edges.description: Persistent receptor tyrosine kinase signaling feeds prolonged flow through the RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK cascade.
Excess RAS-MAPK signaling during development produces the Noonan-like craniofacial, growth, genital, and neurodevelopmental phenotype.
In the hematopoietic compartment, failure to terminate cytokine receptor signaling lowers the threshold for progenitor proliferation.
Prolonged RAS pathway signaling is proposed to disrupt cerebrovascular development, producing progressive stenosis of the terminal internal carotid arteries with collateral vessel formation.
The RAS/MAPK pathway is a major regulator of lymphangiogenesis; its dysregulation produces the prenatal effusion and lymphedema phenotypes shared across RASopathies.
Selective pressure in the hematopoietic compartment favors clones that lose the residual wild-type CBL allele by copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity.

edges.description: Biallelic CBL inactivation in a hematopoietic clone drives the myeloproliferative expansion diagnosed as JMML.

edges.description: Progressive stenosis of the terminal internal carotid arteries with the abnormal deep collateral network is the cerebral expression of this vasculopathy, and can be its presenting and near-isolated manifestation.
The systemic arm of the same vasculopathy, emerging later in life and reported in individuals whose JMML had already regressed.
Disturbed lymphangiogenesis presenting prenatally as fetal hydrops.
The same lymphangiogenic disturbance presenting as fetal pleural fluid accumulation.
Congenital hydrothorax/chylothorax as the postnatal continuation of the same lymphatic drainage failure.
Primary lymphedema of the lower limbs, the postnatal peripheral expression of the same disturbed lymphangiogenesis.
Growth impairment as part of the core germline developmental phenotype of RAS-MAPK hyperactivation.
Developmental delay as part of the same core germline developmental phenotype.
Cryptorchidism as part of the same core germline developmental phenotype, at lower prevalence than in other RASopathies.
The Noonan-like craniofacial gestalt shared with the other RASopathies, which is what places this disorder in that group clinically.
Bilateral ptosis as a component of the Noonan-like craniofacial presentation.
Intellectual disability as one of the neurological features that are comparatively frequent in this RASopathy.

nodes.description: A somatic second hit: acquired segmental uniparental (iso)disomy of chromosome 11q23, the CBL locus, converts the germline heterozygous variant to homozygosity in the affected clone. This is the canonical two-hit step separating the germline developmental disorder from overt leukemia, and the same mechanism has been documented in CBL-associated teratomas.

nodes.description: The germline developmental consequence of RAS-MAPK hyperactivation: impaired growth, developmental delay and other neurological features, cryptorchidism, Noonan-like facial dysmorphism, and ectodermal findings, which the cited series reports as hyperpigmented skin lesions without specifying a lesion morphology. Compared with Noonan syndrome caused by other RASopathy genes, neurological involvement is relatively frequent while cardiac defects, reduced growth, and cryptorchidism are comparatively less prevalent.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline variant in CBL, most often a missense change altering an evolutionarily conserved residue in the RING finger domain or in the linker connecting that domain to the N-terminal tyrosine kinase binding domain. This is the same region mutated somatically in myeloid malignancies; p.Tyr371His is the recurrent hot-spot allele. Splice-site changes, an in-frame deletion, and a nonsense change generating a v-Cbl-like truncated protein have also been reported.

nodes.description: Cbl-family ligases are the dominant activation-selective ubiquitin ligases for protein tyrosine kinases, targeting activated receptors either for endocytic sorting into lysosomes or for proteasomal degradation. When this step fails, activated receptors and their signaling intermediates persist at the membrane and continue to transmit signal.
